description:
NEXUS EARTH is an independent student-led project focused on exploring Earth's interconnected environmental systems through scientific data and technology.

The project aims to develop an interactive tool that uses NASA Earth science datasets to identify environmental trends, visualise changes over time, compare geographical regions and analyse the statistical significance of observed changes.
summary:
**NEXUS EARTH**

NEXUS EARTH is a project I developed to make understanding our planet and its changing environment more interactive and accessible. I wanted to bring important environmental information together in one place so that people could explore what is happening to Earth rather than simply read about it.

The platform features a realistic 3D model of Earth and uses NASA-related environmental datasets to explore patterns in global rainfall, temperature, sea-level changes and heat trends. By presenting this information through visual representations and an interactive experience, NEXUS EARTH aims to help users understand how different parts of our planet are changing over time.

Throughout this project, I worked on researching environmental data, developing the concept, creating the 3D Earth model and building the website with AI-assisted tools. My goal was to turn complex scientific information into something more engaging, understandable and meaningful, while encouraging people to become more curious about our planet and the future of Earth.
details:
About NEXUS EARTH

NEXUS EARTH is a project I developed to help people explore and understand the changes happening to our planet in a more interactive and engaging way. Instead of presenting environmental information through numbers and complicated graphs alone, I wanted to create a platform where users could explore Earth and discover what is happening across different regions of the world.

The platform brings together environmental information relating to global rainfall, temperature, sea-level changes and heat trends using NASA datasets. Through visual representations, users can explore patterns and better understand how our planet is changing over time.

One of the most important parts of this project was creating the 3D Earth model. I used Blender to design and develop the Earth, working on its appearance, textures and atmosphere to make it look as realistic as possible. I wanted the visual experience to feel immersive rather than like an ordinary data website. I also used Base44, AI-assisted tools, and several other coding platforms like Python to help build the website and bring the different elements together. Canva was used to create the presentation and project demonstration.

While developing NEXUS EARTH, I considered accessibility, visual clarity, ease of navigation and how to present scientific information without overwhelming users. I wanted the platform to be useful not only to people familiar with environmental science, but also to students and anyone curious about our planet.

What makes NEXUS EARTH creative is the combination of 3D design, interactive technology and real environmental data. My aim is to make scientific information easier to explore, encourage curiosity about Earth's changing environment and help people recognise why understanding our planet matters.
